Commentary.Commentary: The Australian bowlers were off to an aggressive start, with Hazlewood and Starc applying pressure on the batsmen. Hazlewood kept the run-rate down while Starc was instrumental in taking 3 key wickets. However, the rest of the bowlers failed to impress and didn't create much of an impact. Join us in a bit as the Australians prepare to chase the home side's target down.

Denesh Ramdin was unable to acheive a well-deserved century as Mitchell Starc uprooted his stumps when in his 90's but Samuels went on to 125 in 133 balls, his highest score against Australia in all formats. Kieron Pollard made a brief yet prolific appearance yet his luck was unable to sustain him a second time as he was soon caught out by Marsh. Marlon Samuels remained steady to anchor the lower middle order with his explosive performance, only getting out on the last ball of the innings. West Indies will be very pleased after having successed in setting up a big total of 282 from their perilous position of 31-3 in the first 8 overs.

What a comeback from the West Indians! The innings was off to a shaky start with Johnson Charles getting dismissed in the first over itself. Bravo and Fletcher hold it together for the next six overs, putting up a slow 29 runs, however they were both dismissed in quick succession. At this point, West Indies looked to be in trouble but then entered Samuels and Ramdin to steady the rocking ship. Samuels was the first to start firing but Ramdin soon joined in and the duo proved formidable indeed as they pounded the bowlers around the park. With a mammoth 192-run partnership that lasted 207 balls, the course of the innings was altered for the home side.

OUT! In the air... gone! Samuels departs on the last ball then! What an innings this has been. Walks back with a big smile on his face! Coming to the ball, fuller length ball on middle, Samuels looks to flick but slices it over point where Marsh settled underneath it. That's it, WEST INDIES FINISH ON 282/8!

OUT! Caught! What a start for Starc in his 50th ODI. Fuller outside off, Charles looks to drive it without any foot movement and as a result gets a thick outside edge. The ball goes flying in the slip cordon where Steven Smith grabs it with utmost ease at second slip. Celebrations all around and that is an early wicket for the Windies.
Good length delivery on middle, Charles covers the line and defends it with a straight bat.
Full and around off, Charles looks to drive it through the off side but gets beaten.
Starc bowls a low full toss on the stumps. Charles mistimes his drive towards mid on.

It's time to get underway then. The players and umpires have made their way out to the middle. ANDRE FLETCHER and JOHNSON CHARLES will open the batting for West indies. MITCHELL STARC will start off with the bowling proceedings. Here we go!!!

PITCH REPORT - Damien Martyn feels there is more grass which will assist the pacers and to some extent the spinners as well. Further says, the sun is out and the batsmen shouldn't worry, they just need to get their eye in. Informs 228 is the average score here but he is expecting more than that today.

JASON HOLDER says even he wanted to bowl first. On the wicket, he says it looks a good strip. Adds they don't want to think much, just have to focus on one thing at a time. Admits Australia are a tough opponent but since they have beaten them earlier, they are aware they will come out hard at them. On team changes, he informs SHANNON GABRIEL is making his ODI debut for West Indies.

STEVEN SMITH says the wicket is same just like the last one and hence they will bowl first. Adds knockout games usually brings the best out of the Australian team. Informs they are going with the same squad just like the last one. Ends by saying they are still an inexperienced side and admits these situations brings the best out of them.
TOSS - Holder spins the coin. Smith calls it correctly. AUSTRALIA WILL BOWL FIRST!

However, all will not be lost if the hosts lose as they will still have a chance to make it to the finals in their next match against South Africa. Australia, currently in the No. 2 spot, will be under immense pressure to win this as they stand to get knocked out in case of a loss.The conditions look good so strap for a great match as we get to see who will be heading into the finals!

Hello and welcome to match 8 of the Tri-Nation Series. Today, we will be treated to a clash between hosts West Indies and Australia as they battle for a place in the finals. The previous match between South Africa and Australia was abandoned due to rain, allowing West Indies the chance to make it into the finals if they win.
